`com.google.javascript.jscomp.DisambiguateProperties.FindRenameableProperties.handleObjectLit(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)`

Why:
- Both failing tests revolve around quoted property keys like `{'a': 0}` and bracket access `F['a']`.
- The observed wrong behavior is that property `a` is being added to the rename/disambiguation sets when it should not be.
- Staticaly, `handleObjectLit` iterates every object literal key and unconditionally does:
  - `String name = child.getString();`
  - `Property prop = getProperty(name);`
  - `prop.scheduleRenaming(child, processProperty(...))`
- There is no check for whether the object literal key was quoted.
- That matches the failures:
  - `testOneType4` expected no renamed type set (`{}`), but got `{a=[[Foo.prototype]]}`
  - `testTwoTypes4` renamed quoted object literal property keys (`"Bar_prototype$a"`) even though quoted keys should remain literal and should not participate in disambiguation.

Supporting contrast:
- `handleGetProp` only processes dot accesses (`obj.a`), not bracket accesses (`obj['a']`), which is correct.
- So the bad participation of quoted names is most plausibly introduced from object literal handling, not from getprop handling.

The most likely buggy method is:

`com.google.javascript.jscomp.DisambiguateProperties.FindRenameableProperties.handleObjectLit(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)`

Why:
- Both failing tests revolve around quoted property keys like `{'a': 0}` and bracket access `F['a']`.
- The observed wrong behavior is that property `a` is being added to the rename/disambiguation sets when it should not be.
- Staticaly, `handleObjectLit` iterates every object literal key and unconditionally does:
  - `String name = child.getString();`
  - `Property prop = getProperty(name);`
  - `prop.scheduleRenaming(child, processProperty(...))`
- There is no check for whether the object literal key was quoted.
- That matches the failures:
  - `testOneType4` expected no renamed type set (`{}`), but got `{a=[[Foo.prototype]]}`
  - `testTwoTypes4` renamed quoted object literal property keys (`"Bar_prototype$a"`) even though quoted keys should remain literal and should not participate in disambiguation.

Supporting contrast:
- `handleGetProp` only processes dot accesses (`obj.a`), not bracket accesses (`obj['a']`), which is correct.
- So the bad participation of quoted names is most plausibly introduced from object literal handling, not from getprop handling.

Dynamic verification was attempted on `handleObjectLit`, but the debugger session failed to attach, so the runtime result was inconclusive rather than contradictory.

Best fix location:
com.google.javascript.jscomp.DisambiguateProperties.FindRenameableProperties.handleObjectLit(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)
